tasks.title: Enforce CAMPAIGN_START_V1 before the first external request
tasks.finding: The current capture CLI accepts --source-config and optional --rpc-profiles, creates a runtime manifest, then opens governed transport. The V2 preflight docs say CS-01..CS-10 are mapped manually and no script executes the gate.
actions: Map every blocking CS-01..CS-10 item to an existing code owner and exact pre-network check.
Resolve current canonical human/release authorization mechanism before adding code; inspect src/release_gate/, src/runtime_authority.py and src/provider_governance/.
Require explicit authorization bound to exact approved manifest digest, code/release SHA, source config/generations, RPC profiles, policy, budget, retention and capture window.
Run all blocking checks before constructing/opening external transport or making DNS/network calls.
If canonical operator approval cannot be verified by existing infrastructure, return typed BLOCKED and do not invent an unsigned boolean/string approval that pretends to be authorization.
acceptance: Missing or invalid operator authorization -> typed BLOCKED and instrumented zero physical network attempts.
Changed profile/config/budget/runtime SHA after approval -> typed BLOCKED and zero network attempts.
All CS gates have explicit status, evidence reference, owner and typed blocker.
No CAPTURE_ONLY campaign is executed while implementing this task.

tasks.title: Separate campaign label, cryptographic identity and authorization envelope
tasks.finding: V2 uses a human-readable campaign_id while CampaignManifest.campaign_id is a canonical digest. V2 release.git_commit records ea204222..., older than current main 0a0c8ad9...; campaign_manifest_sha256 is null at authoring time.
actions: Rename the human-readable identifier to campaign_label/campaign_ref and keep CampaignManifest.campaign_id exclusively as cryptographic identity.
Avoid circular self-hash. Use an existing detached approval envelope bound to canonical manifest digest; if no canonical approval owner exists, remain BLOCKED.
Compare actual runtime CampaignManifest to the exact approved manifest before network.
Resolve code SHA dynamically according to release authority; do not hardcode this task's main SHA into runtime code.
Preserve provenance from template -> V1 -> V2 -> approved digest -> runtime campaign identity -> journal/report.
acceptance: A changed manifest or profile produces a different digest and invalidates approval.
Tests cover tampered manifest, missing digest, stale code SHA and dirty checkout.
No null/self-referential identity is ever treated as bound.

tasks.title: Reconcile V2, source catalog, actual adapters and current docs pins
tasks.finding: representative-sources.json has three entries and old 2026-10-06 checked_at values with 86400-second TTL. V2 source names differ from DiscoveryRequest canonical IDs; Meteora adapter is not represented in the current sample config.
actions: Build a four-way crosswalk: manifest id, catalog id, DiscoveryRequest id and adapter id.
Use actual supported IDs for DexScreener, GeckoTerminal, Raydium and Meteora DLMM; aliases require explicit registry mapping plus tests.
Re-fetch official docs, exact route, terms, limits and schema; update checked_at, SHA256, schema fingerprint and provider quota.
Keep all four in discovery-only classification; no indexed metadata becomes an exact edge.
If current docs/terms are inaccessible, status remains typed BLOCKED; do not keep expired pins.
acceptance: All configured source dossiers pass current TTL and schema validation.
Manifest source generations exactly equal the runtime profiles and adapters loaded by CLI.
Positive and negative tests cover alias mapping, stale pin, redirect, 429 and schema drift.

tasks.title: Enforce durable campaign-global physical-attempt and storage budgets
tasks.finding: CampaignEvidenceStore currently exposes per-profile attempt accounting. V2 proposes a global cap of 200 and 100 MiB storage. Verify and enforce both across the entire campaign, all profiles, retries, SQLite files and blob storage.
actions: Keep independent per-provider quotas and add a separate atomic durable campaign-global counter for all physical attempts.
Retries/backoff count as physical attempts; restarts, replay and multi-process workers never reset or double-spend counters.
Enforce the approved total storage ceiling across journal DB, WAL/SHM, raw blobs and temp/staging files.
Fail closed before a network attempt or write if quota/storage usage is unknown or exhausted.
Keep external_data_spend_usd_max=0 and reject paid provider entitlements.
acceptance: Two providers each at 100 cannot exceed campaign-global 200; test concurrency and restart.
Retry counts increment physical attempt count.
Storage usage at the exact limit passes; one byte over fails before persist.
Budget receipts survive process restart and offline replay.

Compare to both registry enums and ensure the intersection supports the exact required read methods.
Do not add unused getBlock/getBlockHeight or unsafe methods just to make schemas match.
Keep every profile disabled/unreviewed until real operator review; maintain 0 network effects in structural validator.
acceptance: A test proves every actual RPC method is explicitly allowed by both relevant registries.
A test proves an unlisted method is rejected before transport.
Sender/submission methods remain impossible.

Optionally add a harness reproducing the pre-fix collision for the record
